hypotheses.justification: Nothing in the statement needs it to elaborate: `M4aHerbrand.IdeleGaloisDescent (𝓞 L) K L` and `L ≃ₐ[K] L` only need `[Field K]` and `[Algebra K L]`. In the whole proof chain (`unitsActHomeo`, `continuous_unitsAct`, `map_unitsAct_eq_smul`, `measurePreserving_unitsAct`), the only use of `NumberField K` is line 175: `haveI : FiniteDimensional K L := Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite ℚ K L`. This is used to show that `σ` has finite order. The other steps depend only on `L`: Haar uniqueness via `isMulLeftInvariant_eq_smul`, local compactness and second countability of the ideles of L, and the compact-neighbourhood argument showing `c = 1`. Without `NumberField K` we can still get `FiniteDimensional K L`, and the statement stays true. Step 1: `haveI : CharZero K := (algebraMap K L).charZero` (`RingHom.charZero` in Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/CharZero.lean needs no injectivity, only `CharZero L`, which comes from `NumberField L`). Step 2: this gives the instance `Algebra ℚ K` (`DivisionRing.toRatAlgebra`). Step 3: `IsScalarTower ℚ K L` holds by the instance `IsScalarTower.rat` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Rat.lean). Step 4: `Module.Finite ℚ L` comes from `NumberField L`, so `Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite ℚ K L` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Finiteness/Basic.lean) gives `FiniteDimensional K L` as before. The earlier lemmas in this file also take `[NumberField K]` as an automatic instance argument but never use it in their proofs. So their proofs can be inlined or copied unchanged, with only line 175 modified as above. Degenerate cases do not arise: K is any field with an algebra map into the number field L, so it automatically has characteristic zero.
